## (3) New finding

### Blocker B-CLOSE — a committed corridorUnion closing whose run vertex is off kerb(F): B-FUZZ red at its fixed seeds (CONFIRMED; pre-existing)

`PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=10000 PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=20261011 corepack pnpm exec vitest run --project kernel --maxWorkers=1
packages/kernel/test/arr/bands/bfuzz.test.ts`, run IN THE TREE: exit 1, `Error: Property failed after 1264 tests`,
shrunk counterexample `[{"a":9517,"b":7960,"hw":27,"knots":null,"ends":"round"},{"a":0,"b":9429,"hw":30,"knots":null,"ends":"round"},{"a":0,"b":0,"hw":1,"knots":null,"ends":"round"}]`,
`"face 1 piece 0 end 1 contact (2699, 3994) pin (2546, 3998): the run's vertex off kerb(F)"` (bfuzz.test.ts:146,
N-57 (2)'s judge `closingsBeyond`). With `PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=1012` (mirror): `Property failed after 3370 tests`,
`[{"a":8489,"b":7960,"hw":30,…},{"a":0,"b":8389,"hw":1,…}]`, `contact (3693, 3985) pin (3586, 3994): the run's vertex
off kerb(F)`. Both runs are byte-identical (log sizes, the 174 REFUSAL lines) on the pre-round `kerb.ts` — the defect
is round S9's engine's (`bandUnion.ts` / `kerb.ts` unchanged on that path), found now because the census was run
through `fc.assert` as well as `fc.sample`; the random-seed NEAR runs (S9, S10, S11, S12 builder, this seat twice) did
not draw such a case, although the fixed seeds meet one per 10⁴ each (20261011 draw 1263, 1012 draw 3369 by
`fc.sample`).

The unshrunk draws, this seat's `close.probe.test.ts` (tree `kerb.ts`):

* **seed 20261011 draw 1263** `[{a 11708, b 7960, hw 29, round}, {a 13806, b 10441, hw 260, square}, {a 15104, b 7783, hw 8, square}]`:
  before the commit face 1's kerb reads `0,896 4000,3783 4000,3931 2362,3977 1853,3983 1538,3986 1735,3817 1689,3764 197,2025 28,1827 0,1851`;
  corridorUnion commits an `along` closing (contact (2362, 3977), tip (2362, 3952), run vertex (1538, 3986)); after
  the commit face 1's kerb reads `0,896 4000,3783 4000,3931 2362,3952 1848,3983 1920,3928 1735,3817 …` — the run vertex
  the closing ran to is **259.6 cm** from kerb(F) as read after the commit.
* **seed 1012 draw 3369** `[{a 10565, b 7996, hw 390, square}, {a 11994, b 7972, hw 29, square}, {a 13848, b 9725, hw 9, knots [362, 58], square}]`:
  face 1 before `… 4000,3943 2693,3986 2251,3991 2273,3964 …`, after `… 4000,3943 2693,3961 2387,3990 2317,3974 2273,3964 …`;
  the closing's run vertex (2251, 3991) **34.8 cm** off the after-commit kerb.

So kerb(F) read at L1 differs before and after corridorUnion's L2 commit (the bfuzz comment's premise "the committed
finer kerb attracts nothing" fails here), and the committed block's closing runs to a vertex the after-commit kerb does
not hold: S8 ≢ S9 on an honest input of the item's own B-FUZZ family — N-45 (a)'s silently wrong committed result, the
item's own bar (B-FUZZ, 0 invalid outputs) red deterministically at its two fixed census seeds. Input kind LAWFUL;
verdict MAKE-IT-SUCCEED (no refusal involved: the commit succeeds with a wrong closing or an unstable read).

**Required change (a fix round of the session's naming):** inside the item's owns, find why the post-commit L1 read of
face 1 moves (the tip (2362, 3977) → (2362, 3952), the run vertex dropped) and make the committed closing and the read
agree (either the read stable across the finer commit, or the closing to a vertex kerb(F) holds) without weakening
`closingsBeyond`; the two draws above as fixtures in the bands tests, red on the present engine; `PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=20261011`
and `=1012` B-FUZZ at 10⁴ green; the census own 0 unchanged.
